newsitem.title: USA: Late-season tropical storm forms in Caribbean.
newsitem.headline: Late-season tropical storm forms in Caribbean.

text.p: A tropical weather system hovering over the Caribbean strengthened to become the 13th tropical storm of the season on Tuesday, prompting Jamaica's government to issue a storm watch for the island.

At 10:00 a.m. EST (1500 GMT), Tropical Storm Marco was near latitude 14.3 north and longitude 80.7 west, or about 360 miles (585 km) southwest of Kingston, Jamaica, and drifting slowly eastward, the National Hurricane Center said.

Forecasters expected a slow eastward to east-northeastward motion during the day. Maximum sustained winds were near 40 mph (65 kph), making Marco a weak tropical storm, but further strengthening was expected during the next 24 hours.
Tropical storm force winds extended up to 70 miles (110 km) from Marco's center.

The hurricane center said a U.S. Air Force plane was en route to check Marco's location and intensity. Western and central Caribbean regions, particularly Jamaica, Cuba and the island of Hispaniola -- home to Haiti and the Dominican Republic -- were told to monitor the storm's progress.

Tropical storm watches indicate that forecasters believe tropical storm conditions could threaten coastal areas within 36 hours. Tropical depressions become tropical storms when sustained winds top 39 mph (62 kph). A tropical storm graduates to hurricane status when its maximum winds exceed 74 mph (119 kph).
This year's Atlantic Hurricane Season officially ends on Nov. 30.
